reuse.why: Builds on the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend, getNextDate, recurConfigToRSchedule and month helpers, extending them with holidays rather than starting new ones.

duplication.why: The 'filter daily weekend/holiday occurrences, then move the rest' pipeline is written separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, with two different look-ahead/window heuristics.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday predicates live in shared/schedules.ts and the new handler in server/schedules/app.ts, matching the tree's layering, though schedule-template.ts still drives the move decision itself.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedule date logic across the four steps, with a small related tweak in rule-utils to carry frequency and holidays.

maintainability.why: There is no single 'final day of an occurrence' function, so the daily-skip vs move rule must be kept consistent in several call sites, and schedule-template's inverted noSkipWeekend flag is hard to follow.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) apply the skip/move decision themselves instead of going through getNextDate's adjustment

disguised_duplication.where: The skip-then-move occurrence logic reappears reshaped in getNextDate (find), getUpcomingDates (filter/slice) and getDatesInRange (filter/map with window), and the window sizing in getDailyWeekendLookahead vs getWeekendMoveWindowDays

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a daily-skip branch (skipWeekendOccurrences/movesWeekend); getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template createScheduleList re-implement the daily-skip/move decision
